title: SF3426 (2019-2020 Regular): Firearms transfers criminal background checks requirement

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/91/2020/0/SF/3426/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version, as filed (undated); official copy from revisor.mn.gov. No passage vote recorded. Struck in the bill: the carve-out for permit-to-carry holders as transferees, the one-year permit and renewal, the identity-evidence rule for unknown parties, and 'pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon' wording (replaced by 'firearm'). The file is long; the rest of section 3 (exclusions, local-regulation and penalty clauses) was read and is not quoted.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 6): (a) A transferee permit issued pursuant to this section is valid statewide for the transfer of a single firearm and shall expire immediately after either: (1) the holder receives a firearm from a transferor, unless the transfer is excluded under section 624.7134, subdivision 6; or (2) 30 days have elapsed from the date the transferee permit was issued to the holder.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 11): A person who makes a false statement in order to obtain a transferee permit knowing or having reason to know the statement is false is guilty of a felony.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 1): Except as provided in this section and section 624.7131, every person who agrees to transfer a firearm shall report the following information in writing to the chief of police of the organized full-time police department of the municipality where the proposed transferee resides or to the appropriate county sheriff if there is no such local chief of police:
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 4): Except as otherwise provided in subdivision 7 or 8, no person shall deliver a firearm to a proposed transferee until five business days after the date the agreement to transfer is delivered to a chief of police or sheriff in accordance with subdivision 1 unless the chief of police or sheriff waives all or a portion of the seven-day waiting period. The chief of police or sheriff may waive all or a portion of the five business day waiting period in writing if the chief of police or sheriff finds that the transferee requires access to a firearm because of a threat to the life of the transferee or of any member of the household of the transferee.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): A person who is not a firearms dealer is prohibited from transferring possession or ownership of a firearm to any other person who is not a firearms dealer, unless the transferee presents a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131 and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 4): (b) A person who refuses or is unable to produce a record of transfer for a firearm transferred under this section in response to a request for production made by a peace officer pursuant to paragraph (a) is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. A prosecution or conviction for violation of this subdivision is not a bar to conviction of, or punishment for, any other crime committed involving the transferred firearm.
